strengths: The paper provides genuinely exact (non-asymptotic) characterizations of REINFORCE estimator variance and NSR for finite-horizon LQG, both in closed form for the one-step case (Theorem 3) and via a lifted-dynamics moment-evaluation procedure for multi-step systems (Theorems 5-6). The derivations are careful, the appendix proofs are detailed and appear technically correct, and the paper is transparent about when it moves from exact results to bounds (Theorems 8 and 11).

The core insight—that NSR is highly non-uniform over policy space and can blow up as the policy approaches a deterministic optimum, creating an inherent exploration-exploitation tension—is a concrete, mechanistic explanation for slowdowns, oscillations, and policy collapse near optima. It connects estimator statistics to optimization dynamics in a way that goes beyond standard uniformly-bounded-variance assumptions.

The connection to optimization is made rigorous where possible (Theorem 4 formalizes escape from any fixed ball when variance grows as 1/sigma^2), and Corollary 7 cleanly shows stationary points of the LQG objective require zero covariance, linking the blow-up to optimality itself.

The ablations are persuasive where they are exact: Figure 7 (larger batch delays collapse; exact gradient eliminates it) convincingly establishes statistical error as the collapse cause, and Appendix B's demonstration that Monte Carlo NSR estimates misrepresent the true trends even with large rollout budgets is a valuable and honest finding that motivates the exact-computation approach.

The paper is honest about scope and limitations: it explicitly restricts to vanilla REINFORCE with Gaussian policies and finite horizons, discusses how baselines/actor-critic and entropy regularization interact with the pathology (including the fragility of baseline cancellation), and clearly flags the open questions (e.g., a formal NSR-instability characterization).
weaknesses: The practical scope is narrow. All exact results apply to vanilla REINFORCE without baselines, whereas essentially all modern methods use baselines, GAE, or actor-critic estimators. The discussion acknowledges that a good quadratic baseline can cancel the blow-up and that only approximate baselines leave the pathology intact—so the practical relevance to PPO/SAC-style training is asserted rather than established, and the paper offers no algorithmic remedy.

There is a methodological tension in the nonlinear experiments: Appendix B shows Monte Carlo NSR estimates fail to capture the true NSR trends, yet the MLP-policy, pendulum, and MuJoCo experiments (Figures 6 and 10) rely on exactly such Monte Carlo NSR estimates to support the claim that high NSR accompanies instability. These results are also only correlational (coupled fluctuations), so the strongest claims about realistic settings rest on evidence the paper itself argues is unreliable.

Much of the qualitative conclusion—that likelihood-ratio estimator variance scales like sigma^-2 and hence grows as the policy becomes deterministic—was already known in essence (the paper cites Zhao et al., 2011, Preiss et al., 2019, Mei et al., 2022, and Ilyas et al., 2018). The novelty lies in exact expressions, scaling with initial-state covariance/horizon/closed-loop stability, and the NSR framing; this is a real but incremental advance over prior variance analyses.

The optimization-dynamics experiments are confined to very low-dimensional systems (2D double integrator, T<=30; two 1D polynomial systems with tiny horizons due to computational limits). The exponential-in-T complexity of the polynomial moment procedure (Proposition 10) limits scalability, and the generality of the observed phenomena across more realistic tasks remains only empirically sketched.

The paper is dense and, at times, difficult to follow: the main text carries heavy notation (IS shorthand, six-term decompositions), key decomposition statements in Theorem 6 defer to equations (38)-(49) in the appendix, and the connection between the abstract Theorem 4 (a scalar recursion) and the actual multi-parameter policy update is loose.
No code release is stated, which, combined with the intricate exact-moment computations, limits reproducibility of the headline experimental claims.
